findings.where: pigment/crates/genai/src/accounts.rs:269-315 (set_default_provider, set_models, set_consented, set_allow_agents, save; also sign_in's save at :189); the interface's direct writes in pigment/crates/ui-egui/src/ai_ui/accounts.rs:575-578 (Act::Timeout), ai_ui/assistant.rs:317 (set_provider) and :340 (set_attach)
findings.issue: Every write of ai.json saves the whole AiSettings the process holds in memory, without reading the file again first. A change another process made since this one last re-read the file is overwritten. That process can be `pigment-cli ai agents off`, `pigment-cli ai consent --revoke`, `ai use` or `ai sign-in`'s hostId. Re-reads happen in status(), admit() and agents_allowed(), but not right before a save. AI Accounts re-reads once when it opens and after each act; the Assistant reads once when it loads. So a window left open keeps an old copy of allowAgents and consented. The next click that saves writes that copy back.
findings.scenario: 1. Pigment is open, with consent given and "Allow agents to run AI commands" on. The person opens Edit › AI Accounts… (or the Assistant window) and leaves it open. 2. In a terminal they run `pigment-cli ai agents off`, which prints "Agents may no longer run AI commands.", or `pigment-cli ai consent --revoke`. 3. Back in the open window they change the request timeout or the Preferred provider, save a model (AI Accounts), toggle Attach image or switch the Assistant's provider. Wrong result: ai.json again holds "allowAgents": true (and "consented": true), and `pigment-cli ai status` says agents may run AI commands. The next ai.generativeFill from an MCP agent or the control channel passes AppBackend::admit or GenAiBackend::allowed (both re-read the file) and is sent and billed, against the person's explicit refusal. The reverse also happens: agents turned on from the command line are turned off again by a click.
findings.test: In crates/genai/tests/genai/keys.rs, using a temp dir: `let mut app = AiAccounts::new(&dir); app.set_consented(true)?; app.set_allow_agents(true)?;` then `let mut cli = AiAccounts::new(&dir); cli.set_allow_agents(false)?;` then `app.set_default_provider(ProviderId::Gemini)?;` and `assert!(!AiSettings::load(&dir).allow_agents)`. Today this fails because the file has allowAgents true again. Write the same check for set_models, set_consented and the timeout. Interface test: open AI Accounts, write allowAgents:false to ai.json from outside, click a Preferred provider radio, and assert the file still says false.
findings.fix: Add `AiAccounts::update(&mut self, f: impl FnOnce(&mut AiSettings)) -> Result<()>`. It calls `self.reload()`, applies `f` (the one field being changed) and calls `save()`. Route set_default_provider, set_models, set_consented, set_allow_agents and sign_in's hostId through it. Replace the interface's `a.settings.x = …; a.save()` sites (Act::Timeout, assistant set_provider and set_attach, generate.rs:228's last prompt and imageProvider) with `a.update(|s| …)`. For a window that stays open this is enough, because the field it writes is the one the person just changed.

findings.where: pigment/apps/photocraft-cli/src/ai.rs:222-231 (AiCommand::SignOut), via AiAccounts::method -> ChatGpt::signed_in (pigment/crates/genai/src/chatgpt.rs:875-880), which returns None while the feature is off
findings.issue: `pigment-cli ai sign-out` decides whether to remove anything with `accounts.method(OpenAi) == Some(Method::Chatgpt)`. That check is false when Sign in with ChatGPT is turned off (`"chatgptSignIn": false` in ai.json, or the documented hotfix `chatgpt::ENABLED = false`). It is also false when an API key is stored next to leftover tokens. In those cases the command prints "Not signed in with ChatGPT." and exits 0, but the tokens stay in the key store, including the long-lived refresh token. The app offers no way to remove them either, because AI Accounts drops the row when the feature is off. The off switch is what FORK.md and PKG-ai-P5 tell the owner to use if the flow misbehaves, and after it the person's sign-in credential stays on disk with no command that removes it. It comes back to life if the switch is turned on again. That can happen without anyone choosing it: AiSettings::load falls back to the defaults (chatgptSignIn true) when ai.json fails to parse.
findings.scenario: Ran here: ai-keys.json holds an "openai-chatgpt" record (access and refresh tokens) and ai.json is {"chatgptSignIn": false}. `PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR=… target/debug/pigment-cli ai sign-out` prints "Not signed in with ChatGPT." and exits 0, and ai-keys.json still holds both tokens unchanged. `ai status` says "OpenAI: not connected". The same happens with ENABLED=false.
findings.test: In apps/photocraft-cli/tests/it/ai.rs, write a sign-in record into ai-keys.json (as ai_sign_in's test leaves one), set "chatgptSignIn": false in ai.json, run `ai sign-out`, and assert that ai-keys.json no longer holds "openai-chatgpt". Add a second case with an OpenAI key stored next to the record.
findings.fix: Base sign-out on what is stored, not on what is active. Add `ChatGpt::has_stored()` (the secret under ACCOUNT exists, whatever enabled() says). In the CLI, call `accounts.sign_out()` whenever it is true (sign_out does not check enabled), and print "Signed out of ChatGPT." Give AI Accounts the same removal while the feature is off, for example a "Remove the stored ChatGPT sign-in" line shown only when has_stored() is true.

findings.issue: `pigment-cli ai set-key` turns terminal echo off by running `stty -echo` as a separate process, and turns it back on only after read_line returns. The CLI installs no signal handler (grep finds no ctrlc or signal-hook). If the person presses Ctrl+C at the "Paste the … API key" prompt, the process dies on SIGINT and the terminal is left with echo off. What they type next into programs in that terminal (cat, a REPL, a password prompt that expects echo) is invisible until they run `stty echo` or `reset`.
findings.scenario: On Linux or macOS in a terminal, run `pigment-cli ai set-key openai`. At the no-echo prompt, decide not to paste and press Ctrl+C. Wrong result: the shell prompt comes back, but `cat` and other programs no longer show what is typed. Bash and zsh line editing hides part of the problem at the prompt itself.
findings.test: A manual check in a pty: script it with python3's pty module. Spawn `pigment-cli ai set-key openai`, send \x03 once the prompt appears, then read termios.tcgetattr on the pty and assert that ECHO is set. Today it is cleared.
findings.fix: Do the no-echo read in a child shell that restores echo itself: `sh -c 'trap "stty echo" INT TERM HUP; stty -echo; IFS= read -r k; stty echo; printf %s "$k"'`, with stdin inherited and stdout piped to pigment-cli. The key goes through a pipe, never argv, and the shell's trap restores echo on Ctrl+C. Alternatively, save `stty -g` first and restore it from a SIGINT handler (rustix's termios is already in Cargo.lock, but it still needs a handler).

checked: Read in full: pigment-genai (keys.rs with FileStore and the chunked Windows/macOS store, http.rs, provider.rs, openai.rs, gemini.rs, image_util.rs, chat.rs, cancel.rs, error.rs, settings.rs, accounts.rs, backend.rs, chatgpt.rs), crates/automation/src/genai.rs with the headless constructors, apps/photocraft-cli/src/ai.rs and the run/batch wiring (document.rs, batch.rs), and the engine's gate it relies on (ai_cmds::may_send, admitted, resolve_provider, ai.testConnection, ai.status). For AI Accounts and the Assistant, only the save and connect paths were read. Checked against the keyring 3.6.3 and ureq 3.5 sources. Ran target/debug/pigment-cli (AI-2 reproduced). Found sound: keys never go in a URL (Gemini sends x-goog-api-key; ureq's debug logging redacts every header it does not list as safe, and no body is logged), and no key reaches stdout, stderr, ai.json or messages: scrub runs before parsing, redact runs after translation, an InvalidKey message leaves out the provider's text, and transport errors carry no secrets. Plan-route tokens: both the refused and the new token are scrubbed, and the code and verifier are scrubbed from token answers. Redirects are off, HTTPS is required except for loopback, and is_loopback resists userinfo, port and backslash tricks. Size bounds: a 64 MiB answer cap with a chunked read and cancel between chunks; the JSON value bound; the decode header check and 24 MP cap before allocation; 1 MiB token answers, 24 KiB JWTs, 8 KiB callbacks, at most 8 listener connections. Timeouts: connect at most 20 s, global from settings clamped to 10–600 s, catalog and tokens 30 s, sign-in 5 min. The CLI sign-in loop cannot hang, because take_outcome expires the attempt. Admission: Agent needs allowAgents; CommandLine needs --allow-ai and is re-checked in prepare after admit; consent is checked before the automatic catalog read; actions, batches and droplets are refused. The CLI's pre-check matches command_list, and the backend refuses nested steps anyway. The keyring features are right (apple-native, windows-native). The chunked store's piece size fits the 2560-byte UTF-16 limit even for non-BMP text; pieces are written in an order that keeps reads safe; a stale count only orphans pieces. The FileStore is written as 0600 and atomically, and its modes are repaired on read. The OAuth callback: the state is checked first, the PKCE verifier never leaves the process (so a hijacked port gains nothing), the HTML page is escaped, and lock order has no cycle (inner is never held across HTTP). Pixel steps: fit_within, pad_to_aspect, crop and resize_rgba8 cannot panic; nearest_size and ratio_of are guarded; the mask conventions are right. The OpenAI and Gemini request shapes match the JavaScript app; Gemini model ids are percent-encoded in the path. Not reported because PKG-ai-final already lists them: a corrupt ai-keys.json reads as empty; nothing was checked live (including whether the plan route's response.completed carries output); Windows echo; Stop does not abort a request. Seen but too narrow to report: two processes refreshing a ChatGPT token in the same instant (refresh-token reuse); a lost update of ai-keys.json between two processes (each key file write is a read-modify-write under an in-process lock only); a describe answer of tens of MB shown in full.
